rationale: Without clear owners and tests, you cannot confidently declare success post-cutover.
evidence: CMDB/service catalog, UAT plans, SLO documents.
red_flag: We do not know who owns some VIPs or no SLOs/test plans.

question: ⛔ If a LB change or failure occurs during migration, what is the tested fallback (bypass, static routing, reverting config, failing to DR site)?
rationale: Lack of a safe fallback makes any LB-related change high-risk.
evidence: DR plans, LB rollback procedures, previous incident postmortems.
red_flag: We have no defined fallback other than making changes manually during incident.

question: Are you currently running Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center), and if so, what version and deployment model (single/HA cluster)?
rationale: Version and topology determine feature availability, scale, and upgrade strategy.
evidence: Catalyst Center GUI About page, platform inventory, data sheet.
red_flag: Single node, non-HA for a large critical environment or very old release in production.

question: Which device families and software versions do you intend to manage (Catalyst 9K, 3K, 4K, 6K, WLCs), and are they all on supported code?
rationale: Unsupported devices or code reduce value of the platform and may block features like Assurance or SWIM.
evidence: Supported devices matrix, device inventory, show version on samples.
red_flag: We expect it to manage everything with many out-of-support platforms.

question: Have you defined the network hierarchy (sites, buildings, floors) and global settings (IP pools, DHCP/DNS/NTP/SNMP/AAA) in Catalyst Center?
rationale: Without hierarchy and global settings, templates and PnP are hard to use consistently.
evidence: Catalyst Center Design workspace, IP pools, network settings screen.
red_flag: We just discovered devices; hierarchy and settings are mostly default.

question: How will devices be discovered (seed IPs, subnets, CDP/LLDP), and have you validated credentials (CLI/SNMP/NETCONF/HTTPS) for all device types?
rationale: Missing or incorrect credentials cause partial discovery and gaps in inventory and Assurance.
evidence: Discovery profiles, credential sets in Catalyst Center, test discovery runs.
red_flag: We will reuse old NMS credentials without validation, or many discovery failures.

question: What is your SWIM strategy (golden images per device family, compliance policies, maintenance windows), and how do you currently manage upgrades?
rationale: SWIM requires clear image standards; otherwise it may push inconsistent or risky upgrades.
evidence: SWIM dashboard, image repository, golden image definitions, current upgrade runbooks.
red_flag: We have no defined golden images or upgrades are ad-hoc CLI only.

question: How are templates and configuration policies organized (project structure, variables, standard switch/router profiles) and who owns them?
rationale: Poor template hygiene leads to drift, errors, and loss of confidence in automation.
evidence: Template editor contents, Git or external repos, automation governance document.
red_flag: Everyone edits templates directly in production with no review process.

question: How do you plan to use Assurance (SLA, Client 360, Device 360), and what telemetry sources (NetFlow, SNMP, syslog, streaming telemetry) are enabled?
rationale: Underused Assurance wastes investment and leaves operations blind to rich telemetry.
evidence: Assurance configuration, telemetry settings, sensor configurations, documentation.
red_flag: We are only using it as an inventory tool with Assurance largely disabled.

question: What is the sizing and resource allocation for the Catalyst Center cluster (CPU, RAM, storage, IOPS), and is it on Cisco's recommended hardware or equivalent?
rationale: Under-sized appliances lead to poor performance, failed jobs, and slow Assurance analytics.
evidence: VM/hardware specs, Cisco sizing guidelines, performance dashboards.
red_flag: We deployed it on low-spec hardware or frequent performance alarms.

question: How do you plan to migrate from legacy management tools (Prime, custom scripts, other NMS) to Catalyst Center, and what will remain outside?
rationale: Overlapping tools can cause conflicting changes and double management.
evidence: Tool inventory, migration plan, operations RACI.
red_flag: We will keep all tools in parallel indefinitely with no clear ownership split.

question: Who in operations and engineering has access to Catalyst Center (roles), and how are RBAC and audit logs configured?
rationale: Uncontrolled access can lead to accidental mass changes or bypassing change management.
evidence: User/role configuration in Catalyst Center, AAA integration settings, audit log settings.
red_flag: Everyone uses a shared admin account or RBAC not aligned to responsibilities.

question: How will you integrate Catalyst Center with ITSM (ServiceNow/etc.) and other systems (ISE, IPAM, SD-WAN controllers, load balancers)?
rationale: Lack of integration reduces automation benefits and creates manual steps.
evidence: API integration docs, existing or planned connectors, workflow diagrams.
red_flag: We have no integration plan or manual ticketing for automated changes.

question: Have you defined standard workflows for PnP onboarding, image updates, and config compliance, and are they documented for the NOC?
rationale: Without standard workflows, automation adoption will be inconsistent and error-prone.
evidence: Runbooks, Catalyst Center task library, internal SOPs.
red_flag: Only a few engineers know how to use it or no written procedures.

question: ⛔ Before using Catalyst Center to push changes, have you tested jobs in a lab or non-production site to validate templates and device behavior?
rationale: Unvalidated automation jobs can push incorrect configs to many devices at once.
evidence: Lab Catalyst Center instance, test job results, change records for pilot sites.
red_flag: We will start directly in production or no lab validation.

question: What is your backup and DR strategy for Catalyst Center itself (snapshots, backups, external database backups), and how long to restore?
rationale: Losing the management platform mid-migration can delay recovery and operations.
evidence: Backup configuration, DR runbooks, restore test results.
red_flag: We do not back it up or Restore procedure has never been tested.

question: How do you track and remediate config drift between what Catalyst Center thinks is compliant and what is actually running on devices?
rationale: Drift undermines confidence in automation and can hide unauthorized changes.
evidence: Compliance policies, config diff reports, documented remediation process.
red_flag: We ignore compliance alarms or no periodic review process.

question: Are you planning to use Catalyst Center for SDA/SD-Access, and if so, what is the migration path from brownfield campus to fabric-enabled?
rationale: SD-Access requires careful staging and integration with existing campus/WAN/security.
evidence: SDA design docs, fabric site configuration, border/control node design.
red_flag: We intend to enable SDA later but have no design yet.

question: What notifications and alerting are configured from Catalyst Center (email, webhooks, ITSM), and who receives Assurance events and failures?
rationale: If alerts stay within the tool UI, issues can go unnoticed by NOC.
evidence: Notification settings in Catalyst Center, integration configs, NOC procedures.
red_flag: We rely on engineers to log into the dashboard periodically.

question: How do you handle template versioning and rollback if a change pushed from Catalyst Center introduces issues?
rationale: Without versioned templates and rollback, operators may hesitate to use automation.
evidence: Template history, Git repositories, documented rollback steps.
red_flag: We edit templates directly with no version control or manual rollback only.

question: Have you enabled and tuned Assurance health scores and KPIs (Client Health, Network Health, Application Health), and how will they feed into operations KPIs?
rationale: Untuned health scores produce noise or false comfort.
evidence: Assurance configuration, health dashboards, operations KPI mapping.
red_flag: Default thresholds only or We ignore Assurance scores.

question: ⛔ For major network changes, will Catalyst Center be the source of truth and change initiator, or will CLI/manual changes co-exist, and how will that be governed?
rationale: Dual control planes (CLI vs automation) cause conflicts, drift, and confusion.
evidence: Operations governance documents, change policy, Catalyst Center configuration mode.
red_flag: Engineers are free to use CLI or Catalyst Center with no policy on precedence.

question: What endpoints and access methods are in scope for ISE/NAC (wired user, wired server, wireless, VPN, OT), and which are explicitly out of scope?
rationale: Scope creep or unclear scope leads to partial deployments and unexpected lockouts.
evidence: ISE design/HLD, endpoint inventory, wireless/VPN design docs.
red_flag: We want to do everything at once or Scope is not clearly defined.

question: Which ISE personas and nodes are deployed (PAN, MnT, PSN), where are they located, and how is redundancy/load-balancing implemented?
rationale: Poor PSN distribution or weak redundancy can cause outages or high latency for auth.
evidence: ISE deployment summary, node map, load balancer configs, show application status ise.
red_flag: Two PSNs in one site only for a global network, or no failover plan.

question: What is the NAD readiness for 802.1X (IOS-XE versions, feature licenses, template availability), and which ports/SSIDs already run dot1x?
rationale: Unsupported features or mixed configs create inconsistent behavior and rollout delays.
evidence: show run | i dot1x, show authentication sessions, WLC WLAN security configs, platform software docs.
red_flag: Only a few closets test dot1x but plan calls for broad rollouts quickly.

question: For each access type, what is the current auth strategy (802.1X, MAB, open) and what is the target mode (monitor, low-impact, closed)?
rationale: A clear mode progression reduces the risk of mass lockouts.
evidence: ISE policy sets, NAD configs, deployment guide mapping.
red_flag: We will go directly from open to closed mode everywhere without phased rollout.

question: How is MAB configured and what profiling sources are used (RADIUS probes, DHCP, SNMP, HTTP, CDP, LLDP, Device Sensor)?
rationale: Weak profiling misclassifies endpoints, leading to wrong authorization and unexpected blocks.
evidence: ISE profiling policies, global profiling config, NAD Device Sensor settings.
red_flag: MAB just dumps devices into full-access VLAN with minimal profiling.

question: What is the certificate strategy for EAP-TLS (CA hierarchy, issuance process, renewal), and how are cert lifecycles monitored?
rationale: Expired or mis-managed certs can cause mass auth failures.
evidence: PKI documentation, ISE certificate store, endpoint cert deployment tools (GPO/Intune/JAMF).
red_flag: Certificates are pushed once with no automated renewal or expiry monitoring.

question: How are RADIUS timeouts, retries, and dead-criteria configured on NADs, and are they aligned with ISE and any RADIUS load balancers?
rationale: Misaligned timers can cause flapping sessions, long login delays, or fail-open behavior.
evidence: show run | i radius-server|aaa, show authentication sessions, load balancer persistence and health configs.
red_flag: Default RADIUS timers everywhere with complex load-balancing or WAN latency.

question: How is RADIUS load-balancing done for ISE PSNs (VIPs, DNS RR, static lists), and what persistence key (Calling-Station-ID, NAS-IP-Address) is used?
rationale: Poor load-balancing breaks session stickiness and CoA behavior, causing inconsistent policies.
evidence: Load balancer config, ISE deployment docs, RADIUS policy configuration.
red_flag: Simple UDP round-robin with no persistence or health probes.

question: Which authorization outcomes are used (VLANs, SGTs, DACLs, URL-redirect, SXP/SGACL) and how are they mapped to business roles?
rationale: Unclear mapping leads to inconsistent security posture and confusion for troubleshooting.
evidence: ISE Authorization Profiles, policy sets, SGT matrix, switch ACL configs.
red_flag: Profiles grew organically with many similar ones and no role documentation.

question: What is the CoA strategy for changes in posture or identity (Port-Bounce vs Reauth vs No CoA), and where could CoA disrupt sensitive devices?
rationale: Aggressive CoA on sensitive ports (e.g., IP phones, OT) can cause outages.
evidence: ISE policy CoA settings, NAD configs, CoA guidance.
red_flag: We always use Port-Bounce on shared/critical ports or no documented exceptions.

question: How are guest and BYOD flows implemented (self-registration, sponsor approval, captive portal), and where are portals hosted and SSL-terminated?
rationale: Weakly designed guest/BYOD can become an operational headache or security gap.
evidence: ISE guest portal config, WLC settings, public cert usage, captive portal policy docs.
red_flag: Guest is a shared pre-shared key or multiple unmanaged ad-hoc guest solutions.

question: What posture checks are in use (AV, OS patch, domain membership), which endpoints are in scope, and how do you handle slow or failing posture checks?
rationale: Overly strict or slow posture checks can delay user access and overload ISE/PSNs.
evidence: ISE posture policies, AnyConnect/posture-agent configs, deployment guide.
red_flag: We posture check everything with no exclusions, causing performance issues.

question: How are ISE logs and live sessions monitored (MnT, syslog, pxGrid consumers), and who in operations responds to auth failures or policy misfires?
rationale: Without clear monitoring and ownership, ISE issues devolve into finger-pointing.
evidence: MnT reports, SIEM integration, NOC runbooks.
red_flag: ISE is a black box or NOC has no access/skills to interpret logs.

question: How is TrustSec/SGT deployed today (inline tagging, SXP, SGACLs on switches/firewalls), and what is the roadmap for broader adoption?
rationale: Partial or inconsistent SGT use can create complex policies and hidden dependencies.
evidence: ISE TrustSec config, switch/ASA TrustSec configs, show cts role-based permissions.
red_flag: SGTs exist but are not used in enforcement or no roadmap.

question: ⛔ What is the fallback behavior on authentication failure (auth-fail VLAN, critical VLAN, open/closed), and is it acceptable for all user and device classes?
rationale: Wrong fallback may either lock out critical devices or unintentionally grant broad access.
evidence: NAD configs (authentication event fail action), ISE policies, deployment guide.
red_flag: Defaults everywhere or Critical endpoints fall back to full-access VLAN.

question: What is the change and rollout strategy per site/closet/SSID (pilot, monitor-only, phased enablement), and how will you measure success/failure?
rationale: Big-bang dot1x leads to widespread disruptions; phased rollout reduces risk.
evidence: Rollout plan, ISE reports, incident stats per wave.
red_flag: We will enable enforcement everywhere in a single weekend with no pilot.

question: How do you manage ISE configuration changes (staging vs prod, export/import, backup), and how often do you test configuration restore?
rationale: Poor change control and backup strategy can lose complex policy logic.
evidence: ISE backup configs, config export files, DR test reports.
red_flag: We rarely back up ISE or Restore has never been tested.

question: For VPN users authenticated through ISE, how are authorization and posture integrated with VPN profiles, and what happens if ISE is unreachable?
rationale: VPN dependencies on ISE without fallback cause remote user lockouts.
evidence: ASA/FTD/VPN configs, ISE VPN policies, AnyConnect profiles.
red_flag: If ISE is down, VPN is down with no backup auth or restricted fallback.

question: For critical non-user devices (printers, IP cameras, OT, medical), which MACs/identities are whitelisted and how are they maintained over time?
rationale: Stale or missing MAC lists cause downtime for critical endpoints when 802.1X is enforced.
evidence: ISE endpoint database, profiling policies, CMDB, OT device inventory.
red_flag: Static Excel file only or unmanaged MAC lists.

question: ⛔ During a cutover to ISE enforcement, what are the exact go/no-go criteria (auth success rates, failure thresholds) and rollback steps per closet or SSID?
rationale: Without clear thresholds and rollback plan, ISE cutovers can spiral into widespread outages.
evidence: Rollout MoP, ISE live logs, show authentication sessions, NOC and app owner agreement.
red_flag: We will adjust on the fly or no quantifiable success criteria and rollback plan.
